issue_context.body:
### The problem

the following error occured in my logs - related to an unhandled exception in the CO2Signal component.

```
Logger: homeassistant.components.co2signal
Source: components/co2signal/__init__.py:115
Integration: co2signal ([documentation](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/co2signal), [issues](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22integration%3A+co2signal%22))
First occurred: 19:45:07 (1 occurrences)
Last logged: 19:45:07

Unexpected exception
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/requests/models.py", line 971, in json
    return complexjson.loads(self.text, **kwargs)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/simplejson/__init__.py", line 525, in loads
    return _default_decoder.decode(s)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/simplejson/decoder.py", line 372, in decode
    obj, end = self.raw_decode(s)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/simplejson/decoder.py", line 402, in raw_decode
    return self.scan_once(s, idx=_w(s, idx).end())
simplejson.errors.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/co2signal/__init__.py", line 115, in get_data
    data = CO2Signal.get_latest(
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/CO2Signal/co2signal.py", line 38, in get_latest
    .json())
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/requests/models.py", line 975, in json
    raise RequestsJSONDecodeError(e.msg, e.doc, e.pos)
requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

@joostlek @jpbede 

Looking at the exception thrown in the issue linked:

```
requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

However, it seems not the exception imported and catched here?
The tests in this PR mocks with the exception (instead of causing the exception), so it is bogus for this specific error testing. The test would be correct, if it actually caused the exception to raise I guess.

Anyways, I'm not sure if this PR is the correct fix.
Although now you mention it, we did not change the test for this one
